reviewerOrPass: Worker B, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the pair, returned to OER articles 3.6–3.8 and 5.8, the annual timetable and official profiling rules. Recomputed the three 60 EC years, reconsidered workbook evidence and strongest feasible candidate schedules, and reviewed the exact exception record.
findings: The degree has 60 EC in each year and 157.5 EC of compulsory study. It begins with tissues, molecules, genomics and physiology before infection, circulation and blood. The second year develops digestion, kidneys, endocrinology, nutrition, skin, neurology, anaesthesia and welfare. Third-year reproductive, public-health, locomotor, epidemiological, multisystem and surgical work continues the clinical and professional sequences. The first-year study advice threshold is 45 EC subject to the stated exceptions. Active participation and course-specific practical attendance apply. Graduation requires passing the courses and the professional portfolio. The 10.5 EC third-year professional sequence includes the 7.5 EC thesis, supervised and marked by at least two examiners. Profiling courses provide 15 EC in year 2 period 4 and 7.5 EC in year 3 period 3. Academic level, approval and non-overlap rules apply. The 7.5 EC outside-faculty requirement in OER article 6.2 applies only to the exceptional free bachelor examination, outside the standard programme. The OER also counts the thesis in its 30 EC description of profiling. It is counted only once in the 180 EC total.

Comparative neurobiology directly supports animal behaviour, welfare and research ethics, while sustainable farming provides husbandry and aquaculture. Infection and Immunity and Epidemiology & Public Health make the One Health option academically meaningful. They do not provide the veterinary study of zoonoses and practical animal welfare across the degree. The stronger anatomy and health-psychology tests confirm human biology and consultation coverage alongside laboratory methods, with the veterinary clinical and species-specific progression still absent. The disposition is based on academic substance.
